title: What If Every Beetle on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every beetle on Earth vanished? You'd lose a quarter of all named species overnight.
There are about four hundred thousand known kinds of beetle, nearly half of all known insects.
Ladybugs would be gone, and the aphids they eat would explode across crops.
Ground beetles that eat caterpillars and weevils would vanish too, so more of those pests would survive.
Beetles also help break down dead plants and animals, so dead matter would pile up much slower to rot.
Take away one insect group and whole food webs wobble. The most successful animal family on Earth holds up more than we notice.
